newsitem.title: UK: Alliance/Leicester, Friends in talks - paper.
newsitem.headline: Alliance/Leicester, Friends in talks - paper.

text.p: British building society Alliance & Leicester has been in talks with Friends Provident on a possible bid but could not agree on price, the Sunday Telegraph newspaper reported.
Spokesmen at neither Alliance & Leicester nor Friends Provident were immediately available for comment.
The newspaper said Friends Provident was thought to be asking as much as 1.5 billion stg, but Alliance & Leicester was unwilling to pay above 1.2 billion stg.
Friends Provident is a mutual life assurer and financial services business.

Alliance & Leicester, which earlier this year decided to opt for bank status, plans to float on the stock market in 1997. Group finance director Richard Pym said last week at the announcement of half year results that conversion would give the society greater flexibility to undertake acquisitions.
But he said there was nothing immediate in the pipeline.
Alliance & Leicester saw pretax profits rise to 183 million stg in the six months to June 30 from 163 million stg previously.
